/Issued 129 PM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

A significant shift from the ongoing mild/benign weather is on track 
for Friday as an upper level trough moving onshore into CA/NV today 
lifts north across MT ahead of an eastward moving trough from 
northern Pacific. 

The trough lifting out of CA/NV will spread unusually deep moisture 
for this time of year (PWATs>200% of normal) north into the area 
tonight through Friday morning with precipitation developing across 
western portions of the forecast area (mainly W of I-15) tonight as 
this moisture is drawn north along a deformation axis across the 
Northern Rockies. This precipitation will be a mix of decaying 
convection that develops over the Great Basin this afternoon with 
additional lift provided by upper jet energy lifting north from the 
Great Basin as well as in advance of the trough arriving from the 
NW. 

The upper trough approaching from the NW crosses the Northern 
Rockies Friday afternoon, shifting the axis of precipitation east 
across the area while also bringing cooler air aloft and lowering 
snow levels before precipitation decreases from west to east Friday 
evening. Cooling aloft will support an initial drop in snow levels 
from above 9000 ft to around 6000-7000 ft across most of the area by 
Friday afternoon, resulting in a change to wet snow over the 
mountains. A secondary push of lower level cooling surges southeast 
out of AB as the northern upper trough axis emerges east of the 
Rockies and with surface low pressure deepening across eastern MT. 
Snow levels quickly lower to 3000-4000 ft across N-central MT as 
early as late Friday morning across Glacier county and by late 
Friday afternoon across eastern portions of north-central/central MT 
and Friday evening across SW MT valleys. Gusty to locally strong 
northwest winds develop with the surge of cooler air across N-
central MT Friday, driven mostly by the surface pressure gradient 
behind the intensifying low to the east. 

Mainly dry conditions follow for the weekend into at least early 
next week with temperatures remaining somewhat cooler than average 
for late October with afternoon temps in the mid-upper 40s and 
overnight lows in the 20s. A more unsettled period may develop by 
mid to late next week as the next trough digging southward along the 
west coast begins to shift inland, though there there is still 
considerable uncertainty with timing and details at this point. 
Hoenisch 

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Precipitation Impacts Tonight Through Friday Morning:

Instances of locally moderate/heavy precipitation rates are likely 
tonight through Friday morning with some embedded convective 
elements and even some isolated thunder possible. 

Precipitation Type and Winter Weather Impacts:

There is still some uncertainty in the how quickly the lower level 
cooling can change precipitation to snow across lower elevations of 
north-central MT Friday afternoon. For most areas outside of the 
mountains, the transition to wet snow will occur with still warm 
ground temps and little opportunity for accumulation before 
precipitation ends Friday evening. Across Judith Basin and Fergus 
counties however there is some concern for the transition to snow 
coinciding with gusty northwest winds and potential for upslope 
enhancement, particularly for near Judith Gap, Lewistown and areas 
from Raynesford to Geyser. With potential for a quick 1-2 inches of 
snowfall occurring near/shortly after sunset Friday and potential 
for gusty winds to add to visibility reduction, winter weather 
advisories were added for these areas.  

Wind Impacts:

Strongest northwest winds on Friday are expected near the Canadian 
border and areas where winds are enhanced near the Island Mtn 
Ranges, particularly the Sweet Grass Hills, Bears Paw, Judith and
Snowy Ranges, where probabilities for gusts in excess of 55 mph 
are 60-80% and a High Wind Warning has been issued. Gusts in 
excess of 40 mph are likely across most of north-cenrtal MT Friday
afternoon, which when combined with temperatures falling to the 
30s will add to the raw conditions for those outdoors. Hoenisch
